newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. agency says Afghan food aid jeopardised.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency says Afghan food aid jeopardised.

text.p: The largest relief agency in Afghanistan said on Thursday that restrictions placed on women by the country's radical Islamic Taleban militia were interfering with its humanitarian work.

"The decision by the Taleban movement to ban women from working outside the home as well as to ban education for girls poses serious consequences for WFP's activities in Afghanistan," the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) agency's executive director, Catherine Bertini, said.

A statement from the Rome-based agency said a bakery in Kabul run by war widows had been closed, leaving some 15,000 people without bread. Some vocational programmes to train women in carpet weaving and tailoring had also been shut down.
Bertini said the most urgent problem, however, was how to prepare for winter when the WFP planned to increase the number of people receiving aid in Kabul from 140,000 to 300,000.

"Because the task of assessing and targeting beneficiaries is carried out by women workers, the added needs, let alone the current needs, can't be met as a result of the recent ban on women," Bertini said in the statement.
The WFP, which is the food aid arm of the United Nations, feeds a total of 1.8 million people in Afghanistan.
Bertini's comments echoed a statement by U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday, warning that discrimination could seriously affect relief programmes in Afghanistan.
